For computed control transfers, the ALU and register-file datapaths produce `reg_dest_val_in`, which becomes `pc_sw` when R0 is the destination or a CALL requests a PC write. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_shift` contributes data or a selector to this computed target; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.inst_alu`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. At the following PC write, execution is redirected to an unintended aligned or misaligned address.

The security-relevant dependency is `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_acc -> openMSP430.watchdog_0.wdtifg_clr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. Instruction fetch is released from `I_DEC` only when `exec_done` or `E_IDLE` is observed, and `e_state` also determines whether jump, source-write, or destination-write completion is pending. `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_acc` controls that execution sequencing before the frontend selects the next PC update; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.watchdog_0.por`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_detect`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. A fault on `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_acc` can falsely complete an instruction or hold the execution machine in an earlier phase when `pc_nxt` is evaluated. The PC is advanced too early, held too long, or updated with operands belonging to the wrong instruction phase.
